title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
core_idea: Drop recurrence entirely; stacked multi-head self-attention + FFN with positional encodings, trained fully in parallel.
why_it_matters: The substrate of every LLM; parallelism over sequence position is what made internet-scale training tractable.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
core_idea: Masked-language-model pretraining, bidirectional, then fine-tune per task.
why_it_matters: Pretrain-then-adapt became the NLP paradigm; held every GLUE record on release.

title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training (GPT-1)
core_idea: Unidirectional (causal) LM pretraining + light task heads.
why_it_matters: Chose generation over masking — the path that scaled into GPT-2/3 and everything since.

title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (GPT-2)
core_idea: 1.5B parameters, web text (WebText) → coherent multi-paragraph text, zero-shot task behavior.
why_it_matters: First public evidence that scale alone induces task abilities without supervision — staged release foreshadowed the capability-safety debate.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
core_idea: 175B parameters; in-context learning — tasks solved via prompts/examples with NO weight updates.
why_it_matters: In-context learning is the property that turned LLMs into a general-purpose interface; launched the entire prompt-based ecosystem.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
core_idea: See domain 01 — power-law loss across N, D, C.
why_it_matters: GPT-3's training budget was set by this curve; scaling became engineering.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
core_idea: See domain 01 — ~20 tokens/parameter at fixed compute.
why_it_matters: Explained GPT-3-class models as undertrained; rewrote every lab's training recipe.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning? (T5: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer)
core_idea: Cast every NLP task as text-to-text; systematic ablations of scale/data/Architectures.
why_it_matters: The field's cleanest ablation study; unified interface precursor to instruction models.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)
core_idea: SFT on demonstrations → RLHF (PPO) with a learned reward model from pairwise human preferences.
why_it_matters: The RLHF pipeline; ChatGPT's recipe. Aligned models differ from base models through this stage, not pretraining.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
core_idea: Learn reward from human preference comparisons instead of hand-crafted rewards.
why_it_matters: The conceptual seed of RLHF, seven years before ChatGPT; also the seed of reward-hacking concerns.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
core_idea: Replace human preference labels with AI feedback guided by an explicit written constitution + chain-of-thought critique.
why_it_matters: RLAIF — supervision that scales with compute rather than human labelers; alignment-as-specified-principles.

title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
core_idea: 1,000 curated SFT examples on a strong base ≈ RLHF-level chat quality.
why_it_matters: Alignment is mostly SURFACE behavior elicitation — the knowledge comes from pretraining; contradicting "alignment teaches capabilities."

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
core_idea: Few-shot exemplars WITH intermediate steps dramatically unlock math/logic at large scale.
why_it_matters: Reasoning as a prompting-recoverable ability; token-space computation begins here → o1/R1.

title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners (“Let’s think step by step”)
core_idea: A single zero-shot phrase triggers stepwise reasoning — no exemplars.
why_it_matters: Reasoning capacity was already in the weights; prompting merely allocates tokens to it.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning
core_idea: Sample many reasoning paths, majority-vote answers.
why_it_matters: Simplest test-time-compute scaling; the "ensemble over thoughts" ancestor of search-based reasoning.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
core_idea: Interleave chain-of-thought with tool/environment actions; reasoning plans actions, observations update reasoning.
why_it_matters: The agent loop — nearly every deployed agent framework (tool use, browsing, code agents) is ReAct-shaped.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs
core_idea: Explore a TREE of thought branches with LLM-guided search (BFS/DFS), value judgments, backtracking.
why_it_matters: Explicit search over reasoning — MuZero's template in token space; big gains on planning-type tasks.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (RAG)
core_idea: Differentiable retrieval into a non-parametric memory (vector index) fused with generation.
why_it_matters: Separates knowledge from weights — cheaper updates, fewer hallucinations, provenance; the backbone of enterprise LLM deployment.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
core_idea: Freeze weights; learn low-rank update matrices — adapter quality at a fraction of memory.
why_it_matters: Fine-tuning democratized (consumer GPUs); weight-deltas as shareable artifacts; the substrate of open-model customization.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
core_idea: IO-aware exact attention — tiling that never materializes the N×N matrix.
why_it_matters: Attention memory wall broken via systems thinking; enabled long-context training; template for kernel-level AI engineering (FlashAttention-2/3).

title: RoFormer: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)
core_idea: Rotate query/key vectors by position-dependent angles — relative positions via complex-rotation structure.
why_it_matters: The default positional scheme of modern LLMs; RoPE-scaling tricks (NTK, YaRN) drive long-context extension.

title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models
authors: William Fedus, Barret Zohar, Noam Shazeer
core_idea: Simplified top-1 MoE routing; trillion parameters with stable training.
why_it_matters: MoE made routine; with Mixtral (2024) and DeepSeek-V3 (2024), sparse routing became the open-frontier default — capability per training-FLOP.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
core_idea: 671B-total/37B-active MoE; Multi-head Latent Attention; FP8 training; 14.8T tokens for ~2.8M H800-GPU-hours (~$5.6M).
why_it_matters: Frontier capability at 1/20th the cost of Western equivalents; engineering recipe ( MLA, FP8, complementary-triangle MoE load balancing) now the open standard.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
core_idea: Chinchilla-optimal small models (7–65B) trained on curated public data match much larger models.
why_it_matters: Open weights + efficient recipe → the entire open-ecosystem (Alpaca, Vicuna, Mistral lineage); weights-as-artifacts era.

title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
core_idea: Optimize preferences directly with a classification-style loss — no reward model, no PPO.
why_it_matters: RLHF-quality alignment with supervised-training simplicity; default in open post-training stacks.

title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning (GRPO)
core_idea: Group Relative Policy Optimization — PPO without a separate critic; advantages from group-relative rewards.
why_it_matters: The RL algorithm that made reasoning-RL cheap enough to run at scale; foundation of R1.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
core_idea: Pure RL with verifiable rewards (no SFT data, GRPO) elicits emergent reasoning behaviors — self-verification, reflection, long chains; test-time compute allocated by problem difficulty.
why_it_matters: The defining result of 2025: reasoning is TRAINABLE BY RL ALONE at scale; R1-distill series moved open models to frontier reasoning; second scaling axis (inference compute) mainstreamed.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can Be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
authors: Charlie Snell, Jaehoon Lee, Sanjeev Raghavan, Avirup Sil (UC Berkeley)
core_idea: On hard math, a small model + optimized test-time search beats a 14× larger model.
why_it_matters: Compute-optimal inference — a NEW scaling law axis; the theoretical spine of 2025's reasoning-model economics.

title: s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
core_idea: 1K curated examples + "budget forcing" (extend/suppress "Wait" tokens) makes a 32B model rival far larger reasoning models.
why_it_matters: Test-time compute control reduced to token-budget steering — embarrassingly effective; reasoning supervision needs are tiny.

title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models
core_idea: On puzzle environments with controlled complexity, reasoning models' accuracy collapses beyond a complexity threshold; effort declines as problems near the frontier.
why_it_matters: The strongest 2025 critique of "thinking" — pattern-matching vs. true search; frames the evaluation frontier (procedural, contamination-free benchmarks like ARC-AGI).

title: In-Context Learning and Induction Heads
core_idea: Identifies induction heads — two-attention-head circuits implementing "copy pattern A→B, complete A→? with B" — as the mechanism behind much in-context learning; forms during a training phase change.
why_it_matters: First circuit-level account of an emergent capability; mechanistic interpretability's flagship (with Nanda's grokking circuit, domain 01).

title: Toy Models of Superposition
core_idea: Networks store MORE features than neurons via nearly-orthogonal directions — polysemantic neurons are a consequence, not a bug.
why_it_matters: Explains why interpretability is hard AND why scaling works (superposition ↔ scaling laws, domain 01 F8/2025 mechanism); foundation of sparse-autoencoder feature research.

title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
core_idea: Sparse autoencoders extract monosemantic features (e.g., "Golden Gate Bridge", "code errors") from polysemantic layers.
why_it_matters: Made features concrete and steerable (feature activation = behavior control); scaling monosemanticity (Templeton et al. 2024) extracted millions of features from Claude — interpretability became an engineering discipline.

title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model (circuit tracing)
core_idea: Attribution graphs trace how individual prompts flow through features and circuits in Claude — planning in poems, multi-step reasoning observed directly.
why_it_matters: (As of 2026) the state of the art in opening the black box; moves interpretability from "what's stored" to "how it computes" — the microscope for F9's emergence questions.

title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
core_idea: On multi-step compositional tasks transformers form parallel "shortcut" circuits whose error compounds exponentially with depth — they don't do serial abstraction natively.
why_it_matters: Explains why chain-of-thought (externalizing steps into tokens) is necessary, not stylistic; motivates search and tool use.

title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration (nucleus sampling)
core_idea: Greedy/beam text is degenerate; sampling from the nucleus (top-p mass) is human-like.
why_it_matters: Sampling strategy is cognition-relevant: model distribution's tail matters; still the default decoding knob in every deployed LLM.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
core_idea: Multimodal, scaled-up transformer; passes professional exams; (details withheld).
why_it_matters: System-scale evidence of continued scaling returns + multimodality; began the closed-frontier era (benchmarks-first disclosure).

title: Advances and Open Problems for LLMs (survey)
core_idea: Analyzes 27 top models (2023–2025): reasoning saturation, data constraints, efficiency frontiers, evaluation crisis.
why_it_matters: Best single map of the field's state as of early 2025 — use as the "what's actually open" reference.
